reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight of the paper lies in modeling agent performance as a function of test-time compute through a Bradley-Terry framework applied to token-budgeted trajectories. Each session's progress is captured as a best-so-far score over increasing token consumption, forming a trajectory S_τ(b). These trajectories are compared pairwise across tasks using Bradley-Terry models, which aggregate into a unified Elo ranking system. The key innovation is that this method allows for cross-benchmark comparison despite varying score scales. The inflection point b_inf identifies the regime where marginal returns drop below 400 Elo per decade, enabling an allocation rule K = max(1, ⌊B/b_inf⌋) that distributes compute optimally among parallel experiments. This approach enables GSE to dynamically adjust model versions and compute resources based on empirical performance trends rather than static heuristics. The framework also supports intervention analysis, showing how strategies like AdaEvolve or TTT-Discover affect performance curves differently at various stages of compute usage. The dual nature of the method—tracking both individual performance and comparative strength—enables robust model selection and adaptive resource management in complex environments.
